entries.label: zero
entries.why: the additive identity and the classic degenerate input; many functions special-case it or forget to

entries.label: one
entries.why: the smallest positive value; off-by-one bugs live in the gap between 0 and 1

entries.label: two
entries.why: the smallest value that is neither identity nor edge; catches 'x > 1' vs 'x >= 1' slips

entries.label: 1e6 (one unit at 6 decimals)
entries.why: one whole USDC in its ERC-20 form; a decimals confusion between 6 and 18 shows up here first

entries.label: 1e9 (one gwei)
entries.why: one unit at 9 decimals, and the gwei scale; a common intermediate a developer might hardcode

entries.label: 1e18 (one whole unit at 18 decimals)
entries.why: one whole token at the standard 18 decimals — the most common single amount in DeFi, and the first round number any tester of a token quantity tries

entries.label: uint8 max
entries.why: the first machine-word ceiling; catches an unsafe downcast to uint8

entries.label: uint32 max
entries.why: downcast-to-uint32 boundary; also the 32-bit timestamp/counter ceiling

entries.label: uint64 max
entries.why: downcast-to-uint64 boundary; a very common storage-packing width

entries.label: uint128 max
entries.why: downcast-to-uint128 boundary; the width DemoVault's own bonus maths would overflow past
one past the uint128 ceiling; the exact value an unsafe uint128 cast wraps to zero

entries.label: uint256 max
entries.why: the largest representable value; forces every addition in the function to its overflow edge
